summary.text: Melvin Rivera is a Brooklyn-born community organizer and tenant advocate running for the open NY-7 seat as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate. According to his campaign website, he has been a community activist for more than 30 years and served in the Mayor's Public Engagement Unit in 2020. He is running on tenant-to-homeownership conversion (TOPA), an anti-flip tax, public safety funding, and an apprenticeship-based approach to public assistance, and describes himself as running independent of party loyalty.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, he was born at Greenpoint Hospital and was raised in Bushwick, Brooklyn, in the 1980s.

Began community work with his first job as a high school student at the YMCA and, per his campaign website, has been a community activist for more than 30 years, working with at-risk youth, seniors, and people with special needs.
Says he helped create tenant associations and cease-and-desist zones in East New York and Cypress Hills, and is helping develop legislation for an Anti-Flip Tax.
Says he assisted families displaced by Hurricane Maria in 2018 with housing, benefits, and employment connections.

Says that in 2019 a management company (Riseboro) mismanaged his rent-stabilized building and neighboring properties into foreclosure, and that he organized tenants across nine buildings targeted by New York City's Third-Party Transfer program, protecting the affordability of more than 150 rent-stabilized apartments.
Served in the NYC Mayor's Public Engagement Unit during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 as a Social Distance Ambassador.
Helped organize community opposition to National Grid's proposed North Brooklyn Pipeline in 2020.

His campaign biography says he experienced homelessness earlier in life and chose to run as an independent; Ballotpedia lists him on the November ballot as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate (also on the No Kings Party and Arts & Culture Party lines), after the Republican primary was canceled.
